pairs.difference: A: ball seen side-on, sitting low-centre against orange dunes with a clear ground/backdrop split; its 0.112 margin is just over the real maximum. B: ball seen from above, filling more of the card with sand as the whole backdrop; its 0.493 area is just over the real maximum. Each misses the range by a little in opposite directions, and both read instantly as a beach ball at thumbnail.

A: target and bear only, inside a plain stall frame that runs almost to the card top (margin 0.019). B: the same pair plus stacked cans, a striped ball and a striped flag post along the shelf, a scalloped light board, a full green brick wall and shelf brackets. At thumbnail the left and right ends of B's shelf fight the target, and the whole stall sits inside the card with a 0.119 margin, above the real range. This matches the lesson lighthouses, where generated cards add side props and pull back to show everything.
pairs.fix: Show only the target and one teddy bear on the shelf. Remove the cans, ball and flag. Move in closer so the stall frame runs off the card edges.

pairs.difference: A: the unit sits top-centre, surrounded by a window and curtain on the left, a plant and books lower left, and a sofa with an orange cushion lower right. At thumbnail the orange cushion and red books pull the eye into the corners, away from the white unit. B: only the unit on a plain striped wall, one clear subject though a little pale. A's added room props follow the generated side of the lighthouse lessons. Measurements do not separate them: both are too short for the real range.
pairs.fix: Show the air conditioner alone on a plain striped wall. Remove the window, plant, books, sofa and cushion.

pairs.difference: A: chest fills the lower centre, with bright gems on the coin pile and a pink shell and loose coins in the bottom corners that pull slightly at the eye. B: chest slightly right of centre with its lid swung right, and paler side props. Area and margins are almost the same (0.466/0.471, 0.071/0.063), and both read instantly as treasure chests. Framing gives no reason to choose.

A: hat fills the card width with a large anchor badge at upper right, reading instantly at thumbnail. B: hat sits smaller and lower-right of the middle, pulled back on the floor, with box height 0.492 below the real minimum of 0.522 and area 0.251 near the bottom of the range. The large dark wall corner and its shadow take up the top of the card and dim the first read.
pairs.fix: Bring the hat much closer so it fills most of the card. Make the anchor badge larger. Keep the background simple and bright.

pairs.difference: A: booth slightly right of centre, tall, close to the top edge (height 0.858, right at the real maximum), with a bright glow behind the roof and a crown pattern around it. B: booth centred and a little smaller, with a faint suitcase pattern. Both are upright and narrower than real cards (0.521/0.512), and both are named instantly at thumbnail. The placement difference is too small to choose on.

A: two whole gloves stand on a diagonal with clear black wrist bands and open cuffs, a clean stripe/floor split, and an instant boxing-glove read. B: gloves lie in a low side-on pile spanning nearly the whole width (0.951, over the real 0.921 maximum), with the right cuff almost touching the edge (margin 0.021). The front glove hides the back one, so at thumbnail it reads as a red lump with the wrist bands nearly hidden.
pairs.fix: Show two gloves side by side on a diagonal, both fully visible, with black wrist straps and cuffs facing the viewer. Leave space between the gloves and the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: large fins sweep corner to corner, with the yellow blades and purple foot pockets filling the card over a bright central glow; width 0.877 is well inside the real range. B: fins are thinner and pulled back, box width 0.516 and height 0.531 both below the real minimums. Their dark grey foot pockets sink into the purple backdrop, so at thumbnail only two yellow slivers read.
pairs.fix: Draw the fins much larger, filling the card from corner to corner. Make the blades wide and the foot pockets a bright purple that stands out from the background.

pairs.difference: A: tight crop, with the jetty running off the right edge, a large rope post at upper left and the life ring as a big red focal point at lower right; only water and sand behind. B: wide scene with a whole jetty on the shore, plus palm, hibiscus, rocks, clouds, a distant island, starfish, shell and sea. At thumbnail the post, ring and jetty are small and share attention with the scenery. This is the same move as the generated lighthouses: pull back and add surroundings, where the real card crops in.
pairs.fix: Move in close on one jetty corner, with the post and life ring large and the planks running off the card edge. Remove the palm, flower, island, clouds, starfish and shell.

pairs.difference: A: thin trunk and slender, spread fronds give little mass (area 0.237, right at the real minimum), so the swirl and the three pale rocks compete for attention at thumbnail. B: bolder tree with a leaning trunk, heavy crown and coconuts, area 0.319, and a single clear dark-green-on-pink shape. This is a mild lean only: both are centred and contained.
pairs.fix: Make the palm thicker and larger, with a heavy trunk that leans, big wide fronds and large coconuts. Keep only one small rock.

pairs.difference: A: locker packed tight into the frame with large books, ball and shoes, area 0.608 and height 0.867, both well past the real maximums (0.475, 0.827). The top nearly reaches the edge and the open door leaves little backdrop, so there is almost no breathing room. B: slimmer locker with visible wall and floor around it, area 0.496 only just over the range.
pairs.fix: Pull back a little and make the locker slimmer, with clear wall visible on both sides and above it.

pairs.difference: A: three-quarter view from above with the slide, yellow platform, blue ladder and water splash all colour-separated, reading quickly. B: lower view of one large green curve with the ramp in the foreground and less colour separation, a slightly slower read. Size and margins are nearly the same (0.39/0.398, 0.026/0.035), and A's height sits slightly past the real range. Neither framing matches a lesson direction clearly.

A: orange device sits small in the upper left (area 0.219) with a blank round button and no symbol, while thin cords and earbuds spread to the lower right. At thumbnail it reads as an orange box with loose white lines, and the eye splits between box and buds. B: larger device (area 0.369) with a white play triangle that names the object at once, and earbuds held near it, though they are large and low.
pairs.fix: Make the music player the large central object with a big white play button on its face. Keep the earphones smaller and close to the player.

pairs.difference: A: flat envelope tilted slightly, with wide-fanned photos and busy colour at top; the stamp is low contrast. B: puffier envelope, tilted the other way, with fewer photos and a strong pink stamp at lower right that pulls a little from the picture. Both sit centred on green rings with similar margins and both are just over the area range (0.428/0.455). Both read at once as mail with photos.

A: flat plate seen from above and tilted on diagonal planks, with a lower, wider shape (height 0.565) and clear space around it. B: fruit piled high in a side view, with extra grapes and a leaf stem at upper right. The plate spreads to 0.949 of the width, past the real 0.921 maximum, with a tight 0.026 margin, so it is crowded against the sides. B's large grapes also compete with the watermelon as lead shape. Weak lean, since A is the less bold of the two.
pairs.fix: Use fewer pieces of fruit, a low pile on the plate, and the watermelon slice as the one big shape. Leave space on both sides of the plate.

pairs.difference: A: whole door shown inside the card, with arch, steps, lantern, flower pot, bush and ivy all around it (margin 0.115, above the real range). The pink flowers and glowing lantern draw the eye to the sides. B: tight crop with the blue door running off the bottom and ivy at the top, so the wreath sits as the clear centre. B's 0.081 area is the wreath alone being measured, not a tiny subject. The door crop matches the real lesson lighthouse, which runs off the bottom edge, and A matches the generated habit of pulling back and adding surroundings.
pairs.fix: Move in close so the door fills the card and runs off the bottom edge. Put the wreath in the middle. Remove the lantern, flower pot, bush and steps.

pattern: Generated cards tend to pull back to show the whole object and then fill the room with extra scenery: side props, palms, lanterns, cushions, starfish. Real cards go the other way, moving in on one subject, often cropping it at an edge. The giveaways are small corner items that pull the eye off the hero at thumbnail size, a hero sitting fully contained with even space around it, and occasional overcorrection into an overpacked card past the real size limits. When both cards are a single contained object on a simple backdrop, framing alone does not separate them.
